landmarks.name: Mount Cameroon
landmarks.writeup: An active volcano and the highest peak in West Africa, popular for hiking and biodiversity.

wiki.extract: Mount Cameroon is an active stratovolcano in the Southwest Region of Cameroon next to the city of Buea near the Gulf of Guinea. Mount Cameroon is also known as Cameroon Mountain or Fako or by its indigenous name Mongo ma Ndemi. Mount Cameroon is ranked 22nd by topographic isolation.

landmarks.name: Waza National Park
landmarks.writeup: A major wildlife reserve known for elephants, lions, and diverse bird species.

wiki.extract: Waza National Park is a national park in the Department of Logone-et-Chari, in Far North Region, Cameroon. It was founded in 1934 as a hunting reserve, and covers a total of 1,700 km2 (660 sq mi). Waza achieved national park status in 1968, and became a UNESCO biosphere reserve in 1979.

landmarks.name: Dja Faunal Reserve
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site, home to one of the largest and best-protected rainforests in Africa.

wiki.extract: Dja Faunal Reserve, located in southeastern Cameroon, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 1987. Causes of inscription include diversity of species present in the park, the presence of five threatened species of mammal, and lack of disturbance within the park. It is managed by Dja Conservation Services (DCS), which is led by a conservator. The Reserve receives significant support for its management from many projects funded by international partners and supporters of conservation in Cameroon.

landmarks.name: Kribi Beaches
landmarks.writeup: Famous for white sandy beaches and nearby waterfalls, a popular tourist destination.

wiki.extract: Kribi is a beach resort and sea port in Cameroon.

landmarks.name: Foumban Royal Palace
landmarks.writeup: Historic palace of the Bamoun kingdom, showcasing traditional architecture and culture.

wiki.extract: The Foumban Royal Palace is a historical building in the city of Foumban, capital of Noun. It is the seat of the Kingdom of Bamum, where the Chief-Superior of the peoples of the valley of the East bank of the Noun resides.

cultural_events.name: Ngondo Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual traditional festival of the Sawa people celebrating their culture and ancestral spirits.

wiki.extract: The Ngondo is an annual water-centered festival held by the Sawa in Douala, Cameroon. The highlight of the festival is a ceremony of the jengu. The ceremony is held at a beach on Wouri Bay, during which a devotee enters the water to visit the underwater kingdom of the miengu. The miengu are believed to be similar to mermaids, and will grant good luck to their worshippers. According to tradition, the devotee can remain underwater for hours, and emerge with his clothing appearing completely dry. Children are not allowed to attend the ceremony. Ngondo was banned by the government of Cameroon in 1981, but reinstated in 1991. The ceremony is held during the first two weeks of December every year.

cultural_events.name: Fête de la Jeunesse
cultural_events.writeup: Youth Day celebrated with music, dance, and cultural performances nationwide.

wiki.extract: Jeunesse Sportive de la Saoura, known simply as JS Saoura or JSS for short, is an Algerian professional football club founded in the town of Méridja in the Béchar Province. They take their name from the Saoura valley of southwestern Algeria. The club was founded in 2008 and its colours are green and yellow. Their home stadium, 20 August 1955 Stadium in Béchar, has a capacity of 20,000 spectators. The club is currently playing in the Algerian Ligue Professionnelle 1.

cultural_events.name: Mvet Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A cultural event highlighting the traditional music and storytelling of the Beti people.

wiki.extract: Music of Gabon encompasses the traditional, ritual, popular and urban musics of the Gabonese Republic. Scholarly literature describes Gabonese musical life as highly diverse, reflecting the country's ethnolinguistic plurality, especially Fang, Myènè, Teke, Punu, Njebi, Kota, Mitsogo and Babongo/Bongo communities, and the close historical connection between music, dance, healing, initiation and oral literature.

food_writeup: Cameroonian cuisine is diverse, featuring staples like cassava, plantains, and maize, with popular dishes such as Ndolé (bitterleaf stew), Eru (vegetable soup), and grilled fish, reflecting the country's ethnic and regional variety.
brief_history: Cameroon was colonized by Germany in the late 19th century, then divided between France and Britain after World War I. It gained independence in 1960 (French Cameroon) and 1961 (British Cameroon), later uniting as the Republic of Cameroon. The country has a rich cultural heritage and has experienced political stability with occasional tensions.

important_people.name: Francis Ngannou
important_people.description: Mixed martial artist and former UFC Heavyweight Champion

current_conflicts: Cameroon faces ongoing conflicts primarily in the Anglophone regions, where separatist movements seek independence, leading to clashes with government forces and humanitarian challenges.
